hook.line: The cooperative's statutes land on Tomás's desk, and the first thing a document like that does is say what the group is made of.
hook.es: La junta consta de siete socios.
hook.en: The board consists of seven members.

examples.es: El examen consta de tres partes.
examples.en: The exam consists of three parts.

examples.es: La junta consta de siete socios.
examples.en: The board consists of seven members.

examples.es: El comité está integrado por expertos de cinco países.
examples.en: The committee is made up of experts from five countries.

examples.es: El reglamento consta de diez artículos.
examples.en: The regulations consist of ten articles.

examples.es: La asociación está constituida por vecinos de La Candelaria.
examples.en: The association is made up of neighbours from La Candelaria.
How many parts does the statute consist of?

rule:
Two ways to say what something is made of.

*Constar de* + the parts: *consta de tres partes*. It is an ordinary verb, so it agrees: *consta* for one thing, *constan* for several.

*Estar integrado*, *constituido* or *conformado por* + the members: *está integrada por siete socios*. The ending matches the thing described: *integrada* for *la junta*, *integrado* for *el comité*. In Colombian texts *conformado* is very common.

English "consists of" and "is made up of" both fit. Both are formal: they belong to statutes, reports and notices.
smallPrint: Teachers call *integrado por* a passive participle: it is the *estar + participle* you already know, with *por* naming the members.

readAndPick.es: El examen consta de tres partes.
options: The exam consists of three parts.
The exam is three hours long.
The exam is on the third part.

readAndPick.es: Los estatutos constan de dos capítulos.
options: The statute consists of two chapters.
The statutes were read in two chapters.
The statutes consist of two chapters.

readAndPick.es: La junta está integrada por cinco asociados.
options: Five members have joined the board.
The board is made up of five members.
The board is meeting five members.
How long is the regulation?
Who wrote the regulation?
How many parts does the regulation consist of?

readAndPick.es: El comité está constituido por expertos.
options: The committee is made up of experts.
The committee is looking for experts.
The committee was founded by one expert.

readAndPick.es: Las reglas constan de diez artículos.
options: The rule consists of ten articles.
The rules consist of ten articles.
The rules were passed in ten articles.

The cooperative is forty years old.
The cooperative is made up of forty neighbours.

options: The decree has several articles.
The decree consists of a single article.
The decree is signed by one person.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *consta* or *constan*: El reglamento ___ de diez artículos. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: El reglamento consta de diez artículos.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *consta* or *constan*: Los estatutos ___ de tres partes. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Los estatutos constan de tres partes.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The board consists of seven members.
yourTurn.answer: La junta consta de siete socios.
accept: La junta está integrada por siete socios.
La junta está constituida por siete socios.
yourTurn.why: *Constar de* names the parts, and *está integrada por* says the same thing.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The committee is made up of experts from five countries.
yourTurn.answer: El comité está integrado por expertos de cinco países.
accept: El comité está constituido por expertos de cinco países.
yourTurn.why: The members follow *por*, and *integrado* matches *el comité*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask: How many parts does the statute consist of?
yourTurn.why: *Constar de* keeps its *de*, so it goes in front of the question word.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *de* or *por*: La asociación está constituida ___ vecinos de La Candelaria. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: La asociación está constituida por vecinos de La Candelaria.
yourTurn.why: After *estar constituido*, the members come with *por*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *El decreto consta de dos artículos.*
yourTurn.answer: Los decretos constan de dos artículos.

pitfalls.wrong: El examen consiste de tres partes.
pitfalls.right: El examen consta de tres partes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Consistir* takes *en* and says what something comes down to. For what it is made of, use *constar de*.

pitfalls.wrong: La junta está integrada de siete socios.
pitfalls.right: La junta está integrada por siete socios.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The members come after *por*, not *de*.

pitfalls.wrong: La junta está integrado por siete socios.
pitfalls.right: La junta está integrada por siete socios.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The ending agrees with the thing: *la junta* is feminine, so *integrada*.

personal: Say what a group you know is made of: your family, a team, a club. *Mi equipo consta de…* or *Mi club está integrado por…*.
